seoTitle: Tailscode — Claude Code & opencode on iPhone, Linux & Mac
metaDescription: Native remote for Claude Code and opencode over your Tailscale network — an iPhone app with Lock Screen Live Activities, plus open-source GTK4 Linux and macOS desktop clients. No relay, no account, GPL-3.0.
heroHeadline: Your coding agents, on every screen you own
heroSubhead: Tailscode is a native remote for Claude Code and opencode running on your own machines — an iPhone app with the turn on your Lock Screen, and open-source desktop clients for Linux and the Mac. Point-to-point over your tailnet, no relay, no account.
highlights: Streams every turn live — thinking, tool calls, subagents, code
Approve, answer, and steer the agent without leaving the chat
iPhone, Linux, and Mac clients built on one shared core
Point-to-point over your Tailscale network — no relay, no tracking

features.title: A real client, not a web view
features.body: Programmatic UIKit on iOS, GTK4 on Linux, AppKit on the Mac — Swift 6 end to end, zero web views. Streaming transcripts with collapsible thinking and tool groups, and syntax-highlighted code with one-tap, byte-exact copy.

features.title: Written, not pasted
features.body: Text leaves a model in lumps, so every client plays the answer out of a buffer at a reading pace: the reveal counts rendered characters and a shimmer wave rides the newest span. Frames come from the display's own clock — CADisplayLink at up to 120Hz on iPhone, GTK's frame clock on Linux — and nothing ever re-wraps under the reader: a frame changes colours, never layout.

features.title: Ultracode wears a rainbow
features.body: Push a turn to the deepest reasoning tier and the app says so out loud: the composer's edge burns with the ultracode rainbow, the effort chip names it, and the presence orb wears the same rim while the turn runs. You can read a session's effort from across the room.

features.title: Three desks, one registry
features.body: Every capability is a case in a shared parity registry, and each client must answer it in an exhaustive switch — adding a feature to one client refuses to compile until all three have decided what they do about it. Nothing ships to one screen silently.

features.title: Two agents, one app
features.body: Drive opencode directly, and Claude Code through claude-bridge — the open-source companion server that turns claude into structured, streaming, subscription-backed sessions with push notifications.

features.title: Lock Screen status board
features.body: A Live Activity per session shows the phase, elapsed time, and tool counts in real time. Approvals alert you, finished turns linger with the outcome, and updates arrive by push even while the app is suspended.

features.title: Steer without stopping
features.body: Queue a follow-up while the agent works, edit it before it lands, stop the turn server-side, fork the conversation, or answer the agent's structured questions with a tap. Subagents open in place; a compaction becomes a seam you can read instead of a wall of summary.

features.title: Seven themes, two faces each
features.body: One catalog shared by every client, from Suomi's aurora-over-a-frozen-lake to fresh snow by day. Every color is pushed through an OKLab contrast corrector until it clears WCAG on its own canvas — a theme that cannot be made readable fails the build.

features.title: The month has numbers
features.body: Every server's transcripts are priced turn by turn and merged into one account: daily bars, the week's rhythm, models, projects, tools, what caching saved — plus a trophy room that scores the same ledger into Game Center.

features.title: The repo, read — never operated
features.body: Branch, drift, conflicts, staged and changed files, and per-file diffs, read from the machine that has to live with them. A chip in the chat chrome spells the tree out the way a prompt does. Nothing offers to commit from your phone.

features.title: One question, from anywhere
features.body: On the desktops a global hotkey summons a quick ask over whatever you are doing — no project, no setup. On the phone it lives in the jump list and Control Center. The answer lands in a real conversation you can pick up later.

features.title: A cue is a meaning, not an amplitude
features.body: Send, step, needs-you, received — each is a composed Core Haptics recipe authored to stay pleasant at the top of the slider: rounded body, soft attack, never an alarm. One intensity dial scales every cue, and a burst of tool calls is felt as progress rather than a rattle.

howItWorks.body: On the machine where you code: opencode serve, or claude-bridge in front of Claude Code. Both are open source and take minutes to set up.
Install Tailscale on your devices — free for personal use. They see each other directly; nothing transits anyone else's servers.
Paste an address or let Tailscode discover your servers. Send a prompt from the phone, follow it on the Lock Screen, sit down at the desktop and the same session is already there.

pricing.footnote: The Linux and Mac desktop clients are free, open-source, and complete — Pro lives on the iPhone, once.

faq.q: Do I need my own server?
faq.a: Yes — that's the point. Tailscode is a remote for agents running on hardware you control. There is no middleman cloud, which means no relay fees, no data sharing, and no vendor outage between you and your code. A built-in demo lets you explore the full app before wiring anything.

faq.q: Which coding agents does it support?
faq.a: opencode natively (any provider you've configured in it), and Claude Code through claude-bridge, an open-source Swift server that exposes Claude Code as structured streaming sessions backed by your Claude subscription.

faq.q: Is there really a Linux desktop client?
faq.a: Yes — a native GTK4/libadwaita app, plus an AppKit app for macOS 26, in the same repository. All three clients share one toolkit-free core, and a parity registry refuses to compile a client that hasn't answered for a capability the others have. The desktops add tiling splits, an embedded terminal, web and video panes, and a global quick-ask hotkey.

faq.q: Does my code pass through anyone's cloud?
faq.a: No. The app talks directly to your machines over your WireGuard-encrypted Tailscale network. No relay server, no account with us, no analytics, no tracking. The privacy policy is one sentence long in spirit: we collect nothing.

faq.q: How do Live Activities update when the app is closed?
faq.a: claude-bridge can push Live Activity updates over APNs, so the Lock Screen keeps ticking — phase, elapsed time, tool counts — even while the app is suspended. Approval requests fire an alert you can act on.

Tailscode Pro is a one-time $14.99 unlock for multiple saved servers, concurrent Live Activities, and a supporter badge. The free app is the complete core — full chat, permissions, attachments, models, forking, themes, analytics — forever, with one server.

All of it, under GPL-3.0: the iPhone app, both desktop clients, the engine (CodingAgentKit, a Swift 6 package that also runs on Linux), and the bridge (claude-bridge). Build it yourself or grab it from the App Store.

faq.q: Can I try it without a server?
faq.a: Yes. Tap 'Try the demo' on the first screen: two sample servers with realistic sessions let you explore streaming, approvals, questions, analytics, and the file browser — no tailnet needed. Every screenshot on this page is that demo wearing the Suomi theme.
